title: Senior Manager – Industrial Data & Manufacturing Systems Integration
text:
Are you looking to power the next leap in the exciting world of advanced electronics?Do you want to help solve problems that drive success in the rapidly evolving technology and connectivity landscape? Then bring your problem-solving, passion, and creativity to help us power the next leap in electronics.
 
 
AtQnity, we’re more than a global leader in materials and solutions for advanced electronics and high-tech industries – we’re a tight-knit team that is motivated by new possibilities, and always up for a challenge. All our dedicated teams contribute to making cutting-edge technology possible. We value forward-thinking challengers, boundary-pushers, and diverse perspectives across all our departments, because we know we play a critical role in the world enabling faster progress for all. Learn how you can start or jumpstart your career with us.
 
 
Senior Manager, Industrial Data& Manufacturing Systems Integration
 
 
**Function:** Integrated Operations& Technology, Digital TechnologyLocation: Wilmington, Delaware, Hybrid (other US Qnity locations may be considered)Travel: Approximately 20–30%Scope: Global, multi-site, and multi-vendor
 
 
Role Summary
 
 
The Senior Manager, Industrial Data& Manufacturing Systems Integration will own the enterprise agenda for industrial data and Level 3 integration across our global manufacturing network.
 
In this role, you will identify, develop, implement, and support two connected sets of systems:
 
 

* The historian and industrial data platform, including EMS/BMS, manufacturing intelligence, advanced analytics and AI, and digital twin capabilities
* The Level 3 integration and middleware layer that supports the platform, including equipment connectivity, edge gateways, orchestration, external-system integration, and twin synchronization

The mandate is to make data contextualization and a standardized edge gateway pattern work at scale. You will bring the architectural judgment needed to make platform decisions and the leadership required to align Manufacturing, Engineering, IT/OT, and external partners. Deep tool expertise will be provided by subject matter experts and specialist hires.
 
 
The Core Challenge
 
 
This role must protect plant-critical data flows and proprietary in-house assets, including custom drivers, tag structures, and site analytics, while establishing sufficient standardization across contextualization models, namespaces, edge patterns, integration contracts, and security.
 
Success requires sound judgment and trusted relationships with plants, engineers, and vendors. The right approach will balance enterprise standards with legitimate local requirements rather than applying a blanket rule such as “everything moves to the cloud” or “nothing leaves the plant.”
 
 
Core Capabilities
 
 
Selection for this role will be based on the following five capabilities, balanced across technical and people leadership. We expect sound architectural judgment, not hands-on expertise in every tool.
 
 
1. Technical Leadership of the Industrial Data and Integration Landscape
 
 
Own the platform decisions, including historian versus lakehouse, integration hub versus custom code, the appropriate edge pattern, and where contextualization should occur.
 
You will frame options; evaluate cost, latency, security, supplier risk, and intellectual property value; engage subject matter experts effectively; and take accountability for the outcome.
 
 
2. Implementing and Supporting Systems in an Operating Plant
 
 
Modernize historians, interfaces, and connectivity that plants rely on continuously without creating data gaps, breaking genealogy, or introducing silent changes to trusted data.
 
You will also establish stable, 24x7 support with clearly defined service levels, controls, and change-management practices.
 
 
3. Stakeholder Engagement and Communication
 
 
Build early sponsorship with Manufacturing, Process Engineering, Quality, Facilities, IT/OT Security, Data& AI, and site leaders across three regions.
 
Explain contextualization, edge technology, and digital twins in terms of business outcomes for audiences ranging from executives to the shop floor. Communicate risks, challenges, and changes early and clearly.
 
 
4. Collaboration Across IT, OT, and External Partners
 
 
Industrial data operates at the intersection of IT and OT and between internal teams and external suppliers.
 
Maintain OT-grade standards for segmentation, edge design, and change control while building effective partnerships with Controls, OT Security, subject matter experts, system integrators, and vendors.
 
 
5. Followership and Change Leadership Across Sites
 
 
Our Wilmington, Cheonan, and Hsinchu sites differ in regulatory requirements, engineering culture, and language. Common standards may encounter legitimate local concerns.
 
Build strong teams, determine what must be standardized and what may remain local, bring sites through the change, and stand behind both decisions.
 
 
Key Responsibilities
 
 
Vision, Strategy, and Architecture
 
 

* Establish the multi-year strategy, roadmap, and ISA-95-aligned reference architecture for the industrial data platform and Level 3 integration layer.
* Govern a fit-for-purpose framework that determines what belongs in the historian, cloud platform, edge environment, integration hub, or custom code.
* Establish data contextualization as an enterprise capability by owning the common asset model, Unified Namespace, and contextualization standards across equipment, process, quality, energy, and facilities data.
* Standardize a secure, outbound-only edge gateway pattern for connectivity, protocol translation, buffering, and edge processing, enabling new equipment and sites to connect efficiently.

Historian and Data Platform Ownership
 
 

* Identify, implement, and support enterprise historians, such as AspenTech InfoPlus.21, including tag governance, retention, high availability, and migration.
* Develop and operate cloud data platforms, including Microsoft Fabric and Databricks, for time-series, contextualized, and EMS/BMS data, with governed data products and access controls.
* Deliver manufacturing intelligence, AI, and digital twin capabilities using platforms such as Seeq, Siemens Insights Hub, Cognite Data Fusion, and Azure Digital Twins.
* Establish the industrial knowledge model and appropriate responsible-AI controls.

Level 3 Integration, Edge, and Middleware Ownership
 
 

* Deploy and support equipment connectivity and edge gateways using technologies such as PTC Kepware, Litmus Edge, Ignition, and Azure IoT Operations across OPC UA, MQTT, SECS/GEM, and Modbus.
* Build and operate the Unified Namespace and contextualization layer using technologies such as HighByte Intelligence Hub, HiveMQ, and MQTT/Sparkplug B.
* Own orchestration and external-system integration using platforms such as Boomi and MuleSoft across MES, historians, digital twins, ERP, PLM, QMS, LIMS, and WMS, including twin synchronization.
* Ensure OT cybersecurity, data governance, and 24x7 resilience for data flows that are critical to shop-floor operations.
* Apply relevant standards and architectural models, including IEC 62443 and Purdue/DMZ principles.

Delivery and Support
 
 

* Own the complete system lifecycle, from business case development through design, implementation, hypercare, and ongoing support.
* Establish service levels, CI/CD practices, and OT-grade change control.
* Manage scope, budget, risk, and benefits across concurrent global rollouts.
* Coordinate platform suppliers, system integrators, and managed-service partners.

Leadership, Stakeholder Engagement, and Team Development
 
 

* Partner with Manufacturing, Engineering, Quality, Facilities, IT/OT Security, MES, and Data& AI.
* Communicate technology strategy, business value, risks, and progress to executive stakeholders.
* Lead change management and adoption at each site.
* Build and develop a global team of architects, engineers, and product owners.
* Add subject matter experts and specialist capabilities where deeper technical expertise is required.

Required Qualifications
 
 
These qualifications represent minimum thresholds and are not the sole basis for selection.
 
 

* 8 or more years of experience in manufacturing IT/OT, including the delivery and support of historian, industrial data, MES, or OT integration systems in semiconductor, electronics, or similarly complex manufacturing environments.
* Five or more years of experience leading distributed teams and multi-vendor programs with accountability for budgets and business benefits.
* Strong command of ISA-95, the Purdue model, contextualization and asset modeling, edge gateway architecture, OPC UA, MQTT, and OT security, with the ability to set direction and effectively challenge technical experts.
* Demonstrated stakeholder engagement and communication skills across audiences ranging from executives to the shop floor.
* A record of building teams and leading change across multiple sites.
* Commercial experience with RFx processes, contracts, licensing, and vendor governance.
* Bachelor’s degree in engineering, computer science, or a related field.

Preferred Qualifications
 
 
The following qualifications may strengthen an application but do not replace the core capabilities and are not intended as initial screening requirements.
 
 

* Experience delivering at least one historian, data-platform, or integration modernization within an operating plant without loss of data continuity.
* Experience taking at least one greenfield or significant new-site deployment through implementation and into stable support.
* Experience in semiconductor manufacturing, advanced packaging, or specialty materials.
* Working proficiency in Korean or Mandarin.
* Experience with technologies such as AVEVA PI, Seeq, Cognite Data Fusion, HighByte Intelligence Hub, PTC Kepware, or Databricks.
* Experience delivering an enterprise-scale Unified Namespace, digital twin, or manufacturing AI capability.
* Relevant certifications such as PMP, SAFe, TOGAF, ISA/IEC 62443, Microsoft Azure, or Databricks.
* Experience in regulated-quality environments, including ISO 9001, IATF 16949, or GxP.
* Master’s degree or MBA.

Technical Environment
 
 
You will identify, develop, implement, and support the systems below while reshaping the technology landscape over time.
 
Many sites currently rely on in-house tools and point-to-point connections. You will determine what should be standardized, rationalized, migrated, or retained where it provides proprietary value. You are expected to understand how the components fit together and make sound platform decisions. Specialist depth will be provided by subject matter experts.
 
 
Historian and Data Platforms
 
 
**Technologies you may encounter or help select:** 

* Wonderware
* AspenTech InfoPlus.21
* Microsoft Fabric
* Databricks

Manufacturing Intelligence and AI
 
 
Technologies and capabilities you may encounter or help select:
 
 

* Seeq
* Siemens Insights Hub
* Azure AI and Copilot
* EMS/BMS energy and facilities data

Digital Twin and Knowledge Model
 
 
**Technologies and approaches you may encounter or help select:** 

* Cognite Data Fusion
* Azure Digital Twins
* ISA-95 asset hierarchies
* Industrial knowledge graphs

Edge Gateways and Equipment Connectivity
 
 
**Technologies and protocols you may encounter or help select:** 

* PTC Kepware
* Litmus Edge
* Ignition
* Azure IoT Operations
* OPC UA
* SECS/GEM
* Modbus
* PLC, DCS, and SCADA environments

Data Contextualization and DataOps
 
 
**Technologies and approaches you may encounter or help select:** 

* HighByte Intelligence Hub
* HiveMQ
* MQTT/Sparkplug B
* Unified Namespace
* ISA-95 asset models

Enterprise Integration
 
 
**Technologies and systems you may encounter or help select:** 

* Boomi
* MuleSoft
* MES
* SAP
* PLM
* QMS
* LIMS
* WMS

Standards and Security
 
 
**Standards and frameworks you may apply:** 

* ISA-95
* Purdue model
* IEC 62443
* NIST Cybersecurity Framework
* OPC UA companion specifications
* SEMI E30 and E164

Living the Qnity Values
 
 
At Qnity, success is measured not only bywhat we achieve, but also byhow we achieve it.
 
 

* Customer: Partner with stakeholders to understand needs, solve business challenges, and deliver meaningful outcomes.
* Innovation: Continuously improve processes, technologies, and ways of working.
* Speed: Act with urgency, focus, and precision to move work forward and deliver results.
* People: Build trusted relationships, collaborate across teams, and inspire positive change.

Join ourTalent Community to stay connected with us!
 
 
Qnity is an equal opportunity employer. Qualified applicants will be considered without regard to race, color, religion, creed, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, national origin, age, veteran status, disability or any other protected class. If you need a reasonable accommodation to search or apply for a position, please visit our Accessibility Page for Contact Information.
 
 
Qnity offers a comprehensive pay and benefits package. To learn more visit theCompensation and Benefits page.
 
 
We use Artificial Intelligence (AI) to enhance our recruitment process.
 
The Pay range for this role is $108,500.00 - $170,500.00 Annual
 
**How Base Pay is Determined:** Qnity has job leveling frameworks that help organize roles based on progressive levels of responsibility, proficiency and qualifications. Each role has an associated pay range (or an established pay rate for some roles) based on the competitive market in each country where we operate. Each individual’s pay is based on a variety of factors, including their role and the associated pay range for that role, their geographic location (i.e., country, state, metropolitan area), as well as their skills, experience, education and certifications, and performance.
